units.text: Aspose.Cells FOSS for Java reads and writes Excel workbooks in the .xlsx format. It creates and manipulates workbooks, worksheets, cells, and cell styles, including formatting and conditional formatting rules. It supports adding data validation and applying style properties such as bold font and custom number formats. The library runs on Java with no external runtime dependencies.

It reads and writes Excel workbooks by loading from file paths or streams into a Workbook that owns a WorksheetCollection of Worksheet objects, and saves the result back to file paths or binary streams.
It applies cell styling and formatting through Style objects that carry font, borders, fill, alignment, number format, and protection flags, set via Cell.getStyle() and Cell.setStyle().
It enforces data validation and conditional formatting on worksheet ranges using ValidationCollection and ConditionalFormattingCollection, both scoped to CellArea.
It creates charts programmatically and preserves chart types loaded from workbooks, and adds drawing shapes with preset geometries.
It configures print layout and page setup via PageSetup, freezes rows and/or columns by coordinate or cell name, and applies worksheet and workbook protection with passwords.

It manages cell comments with author, text, visibility, and size via CommentCollection, embeds images from bytes, streams, or file paths via PictureCollection, and handles hyperlinks through HyperlinkCollection.

This example creates a new workbook, names the first worksheet Report, writes a text label and a numeric value into the first row, applies bold formatting and a custom number format to the numeric cell, adjusts row height and column width, and saves the result as report.xlsx.
The following examples demonstrate validation rules and conditional formatting workflows using Aspose.Cells FOSS for Java.
Create data validation and conditional formatting rules for a range.
The public entry point is org.aspose.cells_foss. The classes below cover the full supported public API surface — 183 public types organized into one module.
The org.aspose.cells_foss package serves as the single public entry point for the Aspose.Cells FOSS for Java library.
It adds additional spreadsheet save formats beyond .xlsx, a full formula calculation engine, ChartEx chart type creation, and dedicated enterprise support.
